name: Q-Transformer
summary: Q-Transformer discretizes each action dimension and predicts Q-values autoregressively per dimension, sidestepping the intractable maximization over high-dimensional continuous actions. Combined with a conservative regularizer and Monte Carlo returns, it trains on large mixed-quality robot datasets containing both expert demonstrations and failed autonomous rollouts, outperforming imitation baselines that must discard the failures.
innovation: Per-dimension autoregressive Q-value prediction, making value-based RL compatible with transformer policies.
Learns from failed data that imitation learning has to throw away.
matters: Points at how large robot datasets full of mediocre trajectories can still improve a policy.
limits: Closed; discretization and autoregressive value decoding are expensive at inference.
lineage: QT-Opt's value-based scaling re-expressed in RT-1's transformer token framework.
